speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what benchmarks are used to measure the quality of healthcare delivery and the adequacy of healthcare resources, such as staffing and infrastructure; and (b) how does the Ministry determine whether our elderly healthcare needs are sufficiently covered by the Pioneer Generation Package and MediShield Life.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: With our life expectancies at birth of 81.9 years in 2015, Singapore residents are not just living longer, but are also enjoying more healthy years of life.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We were ranked first and third in the world for male and female Healthy Life Expectancy (HALE) respectively, according to a 2015 Global Burden of Disease study (GBD) by The Lancet.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There are certainly areas where we can still improve.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In addition to quality of care, the Ministry of Health (MOH) continues to invest in developing healthcare infrastructure, manpower and technology in line with our Healthcare 2020 Masterplan so as to meet our current and future healthcare needs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Through care redesign and adoption of technology, we will further Page: 27 enhance the delivery of healthcare services.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Besides improving quality and access, we have also substantially improved healthcare affordability to provide better assurance, especially to our elderly.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, the Pioneer Generation Package, which many of us are familiar with, provides significant support for Pioneers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MediShield Life now provides lifetime protection for large hospitalisation bills for all Singaporeans, including coverage for the elderly, many of whom were previously uninsured or unable to obtain coverage.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We all know that there are great physical and mental demands on our healthcare workers and this might affect the quality of care provided.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, I am very happy to hear that we will be expanding the healthcare workforce.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Minister consider allocating more funds to manage the well-being and stresses that our healthcare workers will face, especially now with an ageing population?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will continue to work on our journey to transform our care delivery system so that it is more effective and sustainable in the long term.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I mentioned this during the Committee of Supply debate.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are moving from hospital to community: we are moving from quality to value.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the same time, we are also moving from healthcare upstream to health.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These are three key shifts that will make sure that our healthcare, healthcare system and healthcare workers will be sustainable in the long term.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Healthcare, indeed, is a very demanding career but it is a very meaningful and rewarding one.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is what drives Singaporeans to want to join this sector.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I want to take this opportunity to thank all our healthcare workers for their dedication.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But all of us can make their job easier in many ways.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I have shared our efforts over the last few years.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Government has improved the career prospects for our healthcare workers.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Healthcare institutions can also play their part by providing greater support for these healthcare workers, as the Member pointed out, and provide more opportunities and take care of their personal aspirations as well as their needs.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Page: 28 But, more importantly, I believe all of us can play our part, too, whether we are patients, family members helping to take care of the patients or as a general member of the public.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Very often, when we give due recognition to the contribution of the healthcare workers, it will help them in their work.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As I mentioned many times before in this House, a simple "Thank You" card will go a long way in making a healthcare worker's job a lot easier.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I believe that if we work together, we will be able to help our healthcare workers do a better job to take care of our loved ones.
